name: Sensor Prematurity
trigger_conditions: minimum discriminating evidence not yet exhausted
anti_triggers: cheap non-invasive evidence path already exhausted
bounded hypothesis requires instrumentation to discriminate
sensor purpose is directly tied to one admissible decision
physical_basis: Instrumentation only creates value if it discriminates a materially plausible hypothesis.
operational_basis: Teams often deploy sensors before deciding what would actually falsify the leading rival hypotheses.
financial_mechanism: Premature instrumentation creates cost and data noise before the value-of-information path is justified.
typical_false_assumption: More sensors automatically improve diagnosis quality.
hypothesis: Sensor deployment may be premature if minimum discriminating evidence is still cheaper and more direct.
rival_hypotheses: instrumentation is now the cheapest valid discriminator
sensor deployment is required by the decision objective
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: sensor deployment not directly tied to bounded discrimination
falsification_conditions: instrumentation is the next cheapest valid discriminator
sensor purpose is decision-tied and bounded
allowed_claim_language: Sensor deployment may be premature until the minimum discriminating evidence path is exhausted.
prohibited_claim_language: The site needs more sensors now.
financial_exposure_if_false: instrumentation may become admissible once the evidence path is exhausted
stop_conditions: cheaper evidence path exhausted or proven insufficient
escalation_conditions: instrumentation allowed only when linked to a bounded hypothesis and decision purpose
example_outputs: Do not deploy sensors before you know what hypothesis they are supposed to discriminate.
tests: manufacturing and warehouse acceptance bundles should block sensor recommendation while cheaper discriminatory evidence remains available
